article.title: Hit the books
article.description: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).
article.content: Meaning: to study hard, usually before an exam. Example: 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' Register: informal, common among students. Similar idiom: 'cram for an exam' (study intensively at the last minute).

generated.caption:
Got a big exam coming up? Then it's time to "hit the books"! This common, informal idiom simply means to study hard, usually before a test. It's how students often say they need to focus intensely.

For example: "I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test."

Save this idiom for later! Share it with a friend and follow @EnglishVault for daily lessons.

Matlab aaj raat bahar nahi ja sakta, kal ke test ke liye bohot padhai karni hai. Yeh students mein bohot common hai, ek informal idiom hai. Basically kitaabon ko maarna nahi, unko ache se padhna hai. slides.body: The idiom "Hit the books" means to study very hard, usually in preparation for an exam. It's an informal phrase, often used among students. For example, you might say, 'I can't go out tonight, I need to hit the books for tomorrow's test.' A similar idiom is 'cram for an exam,' which means to study intensively at the last minute.
